name: AbsoluteOrientationSensor and RelativeOrientationSensor
plain: Fused device orientation as a quaternion or rotation matrix.
meaning: Gives exact device attitude relative to Earth (absolute) or to its start pose (relative). Same privacy class as DeviceOrientation but easier to use for 3D scenes.

web.api: new AbsoluteOrientationSensor({frequency}); new RelativeOrientationSensor(); quaternion; populateMatrix()

access.prompt_ui: Chromium shows no bubble: access follows the Motion sensors site setting (default Allow) plus the Permissions API name. Safari and Firefox do not ship the API.
access.persistence: Site setting Allow or Block per origin
access.iframe: Cross-origin iframes blocked unless allow="accelerometer"; page must be focused and visible
steps: 'reading' events fire; 'error' event on NotAllowedError or NotReadableError

data.metric: Sensor readings at the requested frequency

limits.headline: Can find which way your device is facing and tilted in 3D
limits.user_action: Nothing in most browsers. Chrome allows it by default unless you changed Motion sensors in site settings
can: Find the device's tilt and facing, compared with the Earth or with where it started
Move a 3D scene, map or AR view as you turn the phone
Give smoother results than basic tilt events
cannot: Run in Firefox or Safari, which do not support it
Show a prompt in Chrome; there is none by default
Know where you are on the map from it
Measure orientation while the page is closed
limits.differs: Chrome, Edge and Samsung Internet support it. Safari and Firefox do not.

story.what_it_is: The page gets your exact device angle, from sensors blended together.

marketing.name: Generic Sensor API
marketing.pitch: Chrome describes a common way for web pages to read motion and environment sensors such as accelerometer and gyroscope.

story.for_you: A 3D scene or map matches the way you hold your phone with no jitter. On many phones there is no prompt. It is the same data as tilt, just smoother.
story.for_makers: Makers use it for smooth 3D, AR and camera control. It has the same privacy class as tilt and motion events, so it can be fingerprinted and can leak typing.

use_cases.example: A browser 3D game or VR cardboard view turns the camera exactly with your head or phone.
A web AR page keeps a 3D model locked to your room as you move.
A map uses full orientation to show a street view pointing where you face.
A virtual tour or 360 video lets you look around by moving your phone.
A tracker records orientation as part of a motion profile.
A site checks for steady human hand motion to catch emulators.

technical_bounds: Absolute needs three sensor permissions, relative needs two

history.change: Orientation sensors ship with the Generic Sensor API
